parsed.explanation: The combined regime is hostile at the national border and uneven locally. National rules make sex assigned at birth the passport/visa anchor, stop new X markers, and direct refusal plus possible lifetime fraud findings where documents or presentation raise doubt; allied governments have issued advisories, and no working border remedy is documented. The state adds a birth-sex facility mandate for schools and colleges (no enforcement mechanism, no documented arrest), narrowed licence markers, and a re-enjoined under-18 care/sports ban whose operative status is unresolved. Custody is the gravest documented exposure: national immigration and corrections practice includes denial of care, forced labour, solitary confinement and sexual abuse, but this is conditional on detention, not routine for visitors. Street violence against trans visitors is not documented; national hate-crime law and local ordinances are patchy protections. Adult-alone and adult-with-minor exposure is driven mainly by border documents; the minor adds unresolved care and school-facility uncertainty.

entry_documents.exposure: National executive-order regime requires sex assigned at birth on passports/visas, bars new X markers, and directs refusal where documents cast doubt; suspected misrepresentation can support lifetime fraud ineligibility. Existing X passports remain valid until expiry.
entry_documents.protection: Court challenges and a legal-aid FAQ exist, but no documented working border remedy for trans visitors is shown.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport meets national screening; any marker/presentation mismatch can lead to secondary inspection, refusal, or a fraud finding.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented national immigration custody abuse of trans men (forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, sexual abuse); corrections policies include conversion-style practices and care denial for trans inmates.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some executive orders are enjoined and legal aid exists, but no visitor-specific custody protection is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border document discrepancy can escalate to detention and immigration custody, with placement and treatment following birth sex.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity; state Protect All Students Act requires K-12 and college facilities by birth certificate, including private institutions.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Single-occupancy restrooms are exempt; the state facility law has no documented enforcement mechanism or criminal penalty, and no arrest under it is sourced.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Applies directly in federal facilities and educational settings; an adult visitor is generally outside school facilities, but campus visits and minors are affected.

care_services.exposure: State under-18 care/sports ban passed, was blocked, allowed, then re-enjoined; status unresolved. National measures target gender-affirming care and insurance. Adult-care rules were withdrawn.
care_services.protection: Courts have enjoined some measures; marriage is recognized regardless of spouses' sex.
care_services.interaction: A visitor seeking emergency or refill care may face identity/document friction; a minor's care access is legally uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National order directs investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; state school-outing law exists.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some court blocks and local ordinances exist.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State rhetoric raises reporting and outing risk in schools and public institutions, but no direct visitor criminalization is documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: State school facility law and school-outing law; under-18 care ban in litigation; national executive order threatens educators. A visiting minor not enrolled has no documented school exposure, but campus/activity access and care are uncertain.
minors_guardians.protection: Single-occupancy restrooms; court injunctions; no documented visitor-minor enforcement.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent may face scrutiny if seeking care or using school facilities; border document rules apply to the minor too.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state statute bars gender-identity discrimination in private employment, housing or public accommodations; local ordinances cover 33 cities/counties. No documented trans-visitor violence pattern appears in the dossier.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; 33 local ordinances; national employment ruling.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse is patchy; police response to trans victims is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport-marker suit, executive-order challenges, care/sports and motor-vehicle marker rules are unresolved; county birth-certificate refusals continue; tier methodology is unexplained.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid guidance, and some injunctions exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A traveller must verify current operative rules; remedies are slow and not shown to change border screening outcomes.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A documents denial of entry but an explicit statutory bar on detention. This dossier has no comparable visitor no-detention shield and documents severe custody harm if detention occurs, so it is less safe.

0.45-A has document mismatch, denial of boarding, no detention, and a weak ombudsman. This dossier adds a hostile national document regime, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, and documented custody abuse, so it sits below 0.45-A.

0.55-B had a supervisor and guideline intervention that waived penalties and allowed travel. Here no working border remedy is documented; court challenges and legal aid do not show outcomes changing screening.
0.75-C shows a patient-privacy directive operating to correct records and issue care. Here care/sports status is unresolved and no visitor-facing care or border protection is shown actually working.

parsed.synthesis: National rules govern entry and custody; state rules add educational facilities, marker limits, and contested care/sports. The sharpest visitor exposure is document mismatch at entry: refusal, secondary screening, possible fraud ineligibility, and, if escalated, immigration custody with documented abuse. Facility exposure is more resident- and student-facing than general-public-facing, but federal facilities and campus settings carry birth-sex rules; the state law lacks enforcement. Protections are real but partial: national hate-crime coverage, local ordinances, court injunctions, and legal-aid guidance, but no documented border remedy actually changes outcomes. Adult alone and adult with minor share the border risk; a minor adds unresolved care and school-facility uncertainty. This is High Risk, not catastrophic, because no trans-specific criminal statute or routine imprisonment of visitors is documented.
